## Data Import

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Load packages and set R Markdown options
library(tidyverse)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)
```

```{r import-data}
# Import the three original datasets
covar <- read.csv("GSE85307_covar-1.csv")

gene_expr <- read.csv(
  "GSE85307_geneExpression.csv",
  row.names = 1,
  check.names = FALSE
)

gene_names <- read.csv("GSE85307_geneNames.csv")
```

## Data Preparation

### Sample Alignment

```{r align-samples}
# Verify sample IDs before aligning the datasets
stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(covar$geoID),
  !anyDuplicated(colnames(gene_expr)),
  setequal(covar$geoID, colnames(gene_expr))
)

# Align expression columns with covariate sample IDs
sample_order <- match(covar$geoID, colnames(gene_expr))

gene_expr_aligned <- gene_expr[
  ,
  sample_order,
  drop = FALSE
]

# Confirm the sample order
stopifnot(
  identical(covar$geoID, colnames(gene_expr_aligned))
)
```

### Covariate Cleaning

```{r clean-covariates}
# Clean continuous and categorical variables
covar_clean <- covar %>%
  mutate(
    mat_age_yrs = as.numeric(
      str_remove(mat_age_yrs, ".*: ")
    ),

    mat_BMI = as.numeric(
      str_remove(mat_BMI, ".*: ")
    ),

    preg_preeclampsia = factor(
      str_remove(preg_preeclampsia, ".*: "),
      levels = c("Normal", "Preeclampsia")
    ),

    BMI_group = case_when(
      mat_BMI < 25 ~ "BMI < 25",
      mat_BMI >= 25 ~ "BMI >= 25",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    BMI_group = factor(
      BMI_group,
      levels = c("BMI < 25", "BMI >= 25")
    )
  )

# Check missing values in the analysis covariates
colSums(is.na(covar_clean[
  ,
  c("mat_age_yrs", "mat_BMI",
    "preg_preeclampsia", "BMI_group")
]))

# Summarize sample sizes across the four groups
count(covar_clean, preg_preeclampsia, BMI_group)
```

## Gene Selection

```{r select-genes}
# Identify genes with probes present in the expression matrix
available_genes <- gene_names %>%
  filter(
    as.character(PROBEID) %in% rownames(gene_expr_aligned)
  ) %>%
  distinct(PROBEID, GENE, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Select three genes for comparison
selected_genes <- c("PTX3", "ABCA9", "ACTG2")

# Find their probe IDs from the annotation data
selected_probes <- available_genes %>%
  filter(GENE %in% selected_genes)

# Verify that each selected gene has exactly one probe
probe_counts <- selected_probes %>%
  count(GENE, name = "n_probes")

stopifnot(
  setequal(probe_counts$GENE, selected_genes),
  all(probe_counts$n_probes == 1)
)

# Display selected genes and their probe IDs
selected_probes %>%
  select(GENE, PROBEID)
```

## Preparing the Analysis Dataset

```{r prepare-analysis-data}
# Extract expression data using the matched probe IDs
selected_expression <- gene_expr_aligned[
  as.character(selected_probes$PROBEID),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

# Transpose expression data so each row represents a sample
expression_df <- as.data.frame(
  t(selected_expression)
)

# Match probe IDs to gene names
gene_order <- match(
  colnames(expression_df),
  as.character(selected_probes$PROBEID)
)

colnames(expression_df) <- selected_probes$GENE[gene_order]

# Move sample IDs into a column for merging
expression_df <- expression_df %>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "geoID")

# Merge expression values with cleaned covariates
analysis_data_2 <- covar_clean %>%
  left_join(expression_df, by = "geoID")

# Verify the merged analysis dataset
stopifnot(
  nrow(analysis_data_2) == nrow(covar_clean),
  identical(analysis_data_2$geoID, covar_clean$geoID),
  !anyDuplicated(analysis_data_2$geoID),
  all(selected_genes %in% names(analysis_data_2)),
  all(colSums(is.na(analysis_data_2[, selected_genes])) == 0)
)

# Summarize expression values for the selected genes
analysis_data_2 %>%
  select(all_of(selected_genes)) %>%
  summary()
```

## Reusable Plotting Function

```{r define-plot-function}
# Define a reusable function for three types of gene expression plots
plot_gene_expression <- function(
    data,
    genes,
    continuous_var,
    categorical_vars
) {

  # Validate the requested variables
  if (length(genes) < 1) {
    stop("Please provide at least one gene.")
  }

  if (length(categorical_vars) != 2) {
    stop("Please provide exactly two categorical variables.")
  }

  required_vars <- c(genes, continuous_var, categorical_vars)

  if (!all(required_vars %in% names(data))) {
    stop("One or more requested variables are missing.")
  }

  # Create a list to store the plots
  plots <- list()

  for (gene in genes) {

    # Plot 1: Gene expression distribution
    hist_plot <- ggplot(
      data,
      aes(x = .data[[gene]])
    ) +
      geom_histogram(
        bins = 15,
        fill = "#5B8DB8",
        color = "white"
      ) +
      labs(
        title = paste("Distribution of", gene, "Expression"),
        x = paste(gene, "Expression Level"),
        y = "Number of Samples"
      ) +
      theme_classic(base_size = 12)

    # Plot 2: Gene expression and continuous covariate
    scatter_plot <- ggplot(
      data,
      aes(
        x = .data[[continuous_var]],
        y = .data[[gene]]
      )
    ) +
      geom_point(
        color = "#5B8DB8",
        alpha = 0.7,
        size = 2
      ) +
      geom_smooth(
        method = "lm",
        se = TRUE,
        color = "#C46A5A",
        linewidth = 0.8
      ) +
      labs(
        title = paste(gene, "Expression vs. Maternal Age"),
        x = continuous_var,
        y = paste(gene, "Expression Level")
      ) +
      theme_classic(base_size = 12)

    # Plot 3: Gene expression by two categorical covariates
    box_plot <- ggplot(
      data,
      aes(
        x = .data[[categorical_vars[1]]],
        y = .data[[gene]],
        fill = .data[[categorical_vars[2]]]
      )
    ) +
      geom_boxplot(
        position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
        width = 0.65,
        alpha = 0.8,
        outlier.shape = NA
      ) +
      geom_point(
        position = position_jitterdodge(
          jitter.width = 0.15,
          dodge.width = 0.8,
          seed = 123
        ),
        alpha = 0.45,
        size = 1.2
      ) +
      labs(
        title = paste(gene, "Expression by Pregnancy Outcome and BMI"),
        x = categorical_vars[1],
        y = paste(gene, "Expression Level"),
        fill = categorical_vars[2]
      ) +
      theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
      theme(
        legend.position = "top"
      )

    # Store all three plots for the current gene
    plots[[gene]] <- list(
      histogram = hist_plot,
      scatterplot = scatter_plot,
      boxplot = box_plot
    )
  }

  return(plots)
}
```

## Generate Plots

```{r generate-plots}
# Generate all nine plots with one function call
all_plots <- plot_gene_expression(
  data = analysis_data_2,
  genes = selected_genes,
  continuous_var = "mat_age_yrs",
  categorical_vars = c("preg_preeclampsia", "BMI_group")
)
```

## Results

### Figure Set 1: Gene Expression Distributions

```{r display-histograms, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
# Display one histogram for each selected gene
for (gene in selected_genes) {
  print(all_plots[[gene]][["histogram"]])
}
```

### Figure Set 2: Maternal Age and Gene Expression

```{r display-scatterplots, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
# Display one scatterplot for each selected gene
for (gene in selected_genes) {
  print(all_plots[[gene]][["scatterplot"]])
}
```

### Figure Set 3: Gene Expression by Pregnancy Outcome and BMI

```{r display-boxplots, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
# Display boxplots with individual observations
for (gene in selected_genes) {
  print(all_plots[[gene]][["boxplot"]])
}
```
